narrative.one_liner: Step up from sliders to code. A single day with a clear evening price peak — write a controller that pre-charges and discharges into the spike.
narrative.teaching_moment: Slider controllers send the same action every step. Code controllers see the live state and can decide. Read `state['price']` and `state['soc']`, return a `battery_flow_mw` that charges when prices are low and discharges when they spike. The template in the Code tab is a good starting point.
narrative.context: Same single-node grid as Tutorial 1, but with a realistic daily shape: cheap overnight power, a midday solar belly, and a sharp 5–8pm price peak. The Simple tab can't win here — a constant battery flow either misses the peak or wastes throughput. Open the Code tab, pick the 'Threshold arbitrage' template, and tune it. Your score is total cost across the day — lower wins.

events.title: Time to write code
events.description: Open the Code tab below. The default controller does nothing — your job is to make it react to price.

events.title: Evening price peak
events.description: Prices spike to ~$0.48/MWh between 5pm and 7pm. If your battery is full and discharging here, you win.
